reviews.decision_reason: demand_selection selects every supplied row because all demand_score values are >=3, but the package supplies only scored need statements and source weights, not observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes. Under the strict demand criteria, this boundary cannot be trusted as demand-bearing selection evidence.

evidence_normalization preserves and bounds the eight selected rows, but it only normalizes fields and filters allowed record identifiers. It does not add or validate market-demand support, so rows lacking observed demand evidence remain visible as unproven demand claims.

provenance_assembly ranks records by demand_score and record_id, causing the downstream recommendation to prioritize the highest-scored unsupported need. Because the scores are not supported by observed market-demand evidence in the supplied package, this is the local behaviorally significant fault that converts unsubstantiated demand scores into the decisive provenance handoff.
